items.title: FPL GW2 EXPERT Transfer Trends & Best Captain! 🧠 100 Experts Reveal Gameweek 2 Team Plans
items.headline: Bruno Fernandes is the overwhelming Gameweek 2 captain as experts hold their transfers
items.summary:
FPL’s leading managers overwhelmingly favour patience in Gameweek 2. Only 4% of the 100 surveyed experts make a transfer, the lowest weekly figure in the series’ history, as most stick with squads built to cover the opening run of fixtures rather than react to one gameweek of returns or blanks. The central recommendation is to roll a transfer unless there is a genuine injury, long-term absence or a specific problem to solve ahead of a Bench Boost.

The limited transfer activity is concentrated among managers using Bench Boost, with moves aimed at replacing doubtful players and improving all 15 squad slots. Caicedo, Richarlison, Morgan Gibbs-White, Pape Sarr and Pascal Gross are the only players sold by experts; Richarlison’s uncertain minutes are a particular concern with Spurs pursuing another striker. Sangare is the only player bought by more than one expert, while isolated moves bring in Cole Palmer, Gvardiol and Varela. A Gibbs-White and Richarlison switch to Palmer and Varela is cited as a team-specific, potentially hit-taking route rather than a broadly endorsed play.

The experts resist the wider-market rush towards Brighton defender Maxim De Cuyper after his Gameweek 1 goal, particularly with Chelsea away next. No surveyed manager buys him despite just 1% expert ownership, underlining the reluctance to chase a single attacking return from a defender. The same applies to popular budget options such as Caicedo and Rogers: a lack of expert ownership does not automatically make them transfer targets. Meanwhile, heavily owned picks including Joao Pedro, Calafiori and Solanke attract little expert buying because many leading managers already hold them.

Bench Boost is the only chip in play. After 56% of experts use it in Gameweek 1, another 25% deploy it in Gameweek 2, leaving only 19% with the chip afterwards. No Triple Captain, Free Hit or Wildcard is used. For managers with a strong bench, Gameweek 2 remains a possible Bench Boost window; otherwise, preserving the squad structure and banked transfer is preferred.

Captaincy is far clearer: Bruno Fernandes leads the way for Ipswich at home, backed by 75% of all experts and 83% of his owners. Erling Haaland is the credible alternative, selected by 20% overall and 25% of his owners, so backing him is a viable differential rather than a rogue call. Small minorities captain Ekitike, Bryan Mbeumo or Joao Pedro. The broader message is that experts retain faith in proven assets after Gameweek 1 blanks: they keep Mbeumo and Ekitike rather than sell them, and some even hand them the armband.
key_points: Only 4% of experts make a Gameweek 2 transfer, so rolling is the default unless an injury, long-term absence or Bench Boost issue demands action.
Bruno Fernandes is the dominant captain for Ipswich at home, with 75% overall expert backing and an 83% captaincy rate among his owners.
Erling Haaland receives 20% of expert captaincies, making him the main alternative to Fernandes rather than an extreme differential.
Bench Boost remains the only active chip: 56% use it in Gameweek 1 and a further 25% use it in Gameweek 2.
Transfers are largely Bench Boost-driven, with Caicedo, Richarlison, Morgan Gibbs-White, Pape Sarr and Pascal Gross among the few expert sales.
Experts do not chase Brighton defender Maxim De Cuyper’s Gameweek 1 goal ahead of Chelsea away, despite heavy buying from the wider player base.
Richarlison is a minutes risk as Spurs seek another striker, while Mbeumo and Ekitike retain expert backing despite wider-market sales.

items.title: MY TOP 3 FPL GW2 PLAYERS TO BUY! 💰 #premierleague #fpl
items.headline: Arsenal defensive double-up tops Gameweek 2 transfer watchlist
items.summary:
Arsenal’s defence is the standout area to target ahead of Gameweek 2. Riccardo Calafiori is already in place, but adding Ben White alongside him is under consideration if funds allow, with Arsenal looking strong enough at the back to justify a defensive double-up. The likely route is moving on Harry Maguire, who is unconvincing in Gameweek 1, although the switch is viewed more as a move for the coming weeks than an urgent transfer for this round.

In midfield, Sangare emerges as an early attacking option after a 14-point return. He looks heavily involved in Brentford’s attacking play and central to their chances of producing goals and assists, making him a player to monitor as managers assess whether his Gameweek 1 output is sustainable.

Up front, Newcastle’s upcoming schedule is the main attraction, with a favourable run stretching across roughly the next eight Gameweeks. Yoane Wissa impresses against Liverpool and is on the radar as a forward target, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the potential sacrifice after failing to convince in Gameweek 1. The recommendation is to keep close watch on Newcastle’s forward options rather than force an immediate move without further evidence.
key_points: Arsenal’s defensive strength makes a double-up, led by Ben White alongside Riccardo Calafiori, an appealing medium-term plan.
Harry Maguire is the likely player to make way, but the Arsenal defensive move is not necessarily urgent for Gameweek 2.
Sangare becomes a midfield watchlist option after scoring 14 points and looking central to Brentford’s attack.
Newcastle have a favourable fixture run for around the next eight Gameweeks, increasing the appeal of their forwards.
Yoane Wissa is a forward to monitor after an impressive display against Liverpool.
Dominic Calvert-Lewin is under pressure as a squad place after a poor Gameweek 1 showing.

items.title: FPL GW2 Transfer Tips! | Buy, Sell, Keep, Avoid #fpl
items.headline: Buy William Saliba and move on from Pedro Porro for Gameweek 2
items.summary:
William Saliba is the leading Gameweek 2 buy after Arsenal open the season with a clean sheet. At £5.5m, he offers a reliable route into a defence expected to address the clean-sheet concerns facing many managers, while retaining some attacking upside. Ben White is also appealing for managers considering an Arsenal defensive double-up.

Pedro Porro is the recommended sale. He is not yet fully fit, Tottenham begin with an unconvincing performance, and their revamped defence may need time to settle. At £5.5m, Porro looks poor value if clean sheets remain uncertain, while James Maddison’s expected return from injury could reduce Porro’s set-piece involvement and attacking appeal.

Bryan Mbeumo is a hold despite Manchester United’s disappointing opening display. United are expected to respond at home to Ipswich Town in Gameweek 2, and Mbeumo is their clearest attacking threat in the first match. His 0.72 expected goal involvement is among the strongest underlying numbers of the gameweek, suggesting he is unlucky not to return after being denied by the opposition goalkeeper.

Maxim De Cuyper is worth avoiding as a new purchase for one more week. He excels against an unprepared Aston Villa in Gameweek 1, but an away trip to a free-scoring Chelsea is a much tougher assignment and carries clean-sheet risk for a defender. His attacking returns are not guaranteed every week, and many existing owners are likely to bench him; managers without him can wait for his fixtures to improve dramatically after Gameweek 2.
key_points: Buy William Saliba at £5.5m after Arsenal’s opening clean sheet, with Ben White also viable for a defensive double-up.
Sell Pedro Porro, whose fitness, Tottenham’s defensive uncertainty and likely loss of set pieces to James Maddison weaken his £5.5m appeal.
Keep Bryan Mbeumo for Manchester United’s Gameweek 2 home match against Ipswich Town after he posts 0.72 expected goal involvement in the opener.
Avoid buying Maxim De Cuyper before his Gameweek 2 trip to Chelsea, where clean-sheet prospects are limited.
De Cuyper remains a longer-term option, but non-owners can wait a week for a significantly better fixture run.

items.title: My FPL GW2 TEAM 🔥 Gameweek 2 ✅
items.headline: Bruno Fernandes remains captain despite Gameweek 1 blank as Manchester United target Ipswich response
items.summary:
A 60-point Bench Boost in Gameweek 1 feels underwhelming after blanks from Bruno Fernandes and Erling Haaland, but it remains a solid start and there is no need for an early overreaction. The key regret is bypassing João Pedro, although that saving funded Ben White, whose 11 points match João Pedro’s output. The White-and-Brobbey combination still has two more Gameweeks to justify itself before a likely Wildcard.

The Gameweek 2 starting XI is Kinsky; Riccardo Calafiori, Harry Maguire and White; Bryan Mbeumo, Bruno, Dominik Szoboszlai and Zolas; Brobbey, Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Haaland. Kinsky faces Newcastle after Tottenham concede more expected goals than any side in Gameweek 1, so he is not an especially attractive clean-sheet pick, but the defence is otherwise strong. Manchester United and Arsenal lead the clean-sheet odds at 42%, while Liverpool are at 38% and Manchester City at 36%. White is particularly appealing against an understrength Aston Villa, who may again be without Ollie Watkins and are vulnerable down their left flank.

Bruno keeps the armband at home to Ipswich despite his opening blank. Manchester United look poor against Hull, but Ipswich at Old Trafford remains a prime fixture and the expectation is for a sharp response. Haaland is a credible alternative, especially against a Crystal Palace side dealing with injuries and uncertainty around Eberechi Eze, but Bruno rates as the top captain in the captaincy model. Mbeumo and Bruno are retained because Manchester United have a favourable fixture and no midweek match, while Szoboszlai gains further appeal after taking a penalty against Newcastle and appearing to be involved in Liverpool’s set pieces. Zolas also looks secure for Arsenal while Gabriel Martinelli appears likely to leave.

No transfer is needed for Gameweek 2, so the plan is to roll and enter Gameweek 3 with two free transfers. That creates flexibility to move Mbeumo to a Manchester City midfielder such as Cherki or Phil Foden if either impresses, or to consider Bruno to Semenyo if he looks explosive. An Arsenal defender for Vardio is another potential move ahead of Arsenal’s home match against Chelsea. Haaland is central to the strategy: no-Haaland squads make a strong start, often with deeper benches, but the premium striker needs a major return against Palace to reward the decision to retain him.
key_points: Bruno Fernandes is the Gameweek 2 captain against Ipswich, with Haaland the main alternative against Crystal Palace.
The squad rolls its transfer in Gameweek 2, preserving two free transfers for Gameweek 3 decisions.
Manchester United and Arsenal lead the Gameweek 2 clean-sheet odds at 42%, supporting Maguire, Calafiori and Ben White.
White is favoured against a potentially Watkins-less Aston Villa, while Arsenal’s right side could exploit Villa’s weakened left flank.
Szoboszlai becomes a stronger midfield pick after taking Liverpool’s penalty and standing over corners and free kicks.
Mbeumo and Bruno stay despite Gameweek 1 blanks, with a judgement on a possible Manchester City midfield switch deferred until Gameweek 3.
Haaland’s fixture against a troubled Crystal Palace makes this a crucial week for Haaland drafts to gain ground on no-Haaland teams.
Sangari and Diaper rise in price after Gameweek 1, while Martinelli and Gyökeres fall.

items.title: FPL Gameweek 2 Preview 🔥 Bruno captain 😬 Buy Wissa 🤔
items.headline: Bruno Fernandes remains the Gameweek 2 captain ahead of Haaland and Palmer
items.summary:
Bruno Fernandes is the preferred captain for Gameweek 2 despite Manchester United losing to Hull in the opening round. Ipswich at home remains one of United's best fixtures of the season and newly promoted sides should still be targeted until a sustained run of evidence says otherwise. Erling Haaland away at Crystal Palace is never a bad choice and should still receive regular captaincy later on, but this is viewed as a week to oppose him. Cole Palmer, at home to Brighton, is the leading differential after an impressive display against Fulham and likely penalty duty, although managers should check Friday's update after he leaves the pitch with a possible minor knock. Bukayo Saka against Aston Villa is another differential, but his expected 70-minute outings and uncertain penalty share with Jorginho make him less attractive.

One Gameweek should inform decisions without overturning pre-season plans. Arsenal look strong, Aston Villa look vulnerable, De Cuyper is playing as a 4.5m left-sided defender with set-piece involvement, and Sangare's Brentford start is encouraging for his minutes. But De Cuyper should probably still be benched at Chelsea if the alternatives are Maguire against Ipswich, Ballard against Fulham or Calafiori against Villa, because clean-sheet potential remains more reliable than an out-of-position defender's attacking upside. The performance does, however, make De Cuyper worth retaining longer than originally planned. Zolis versus Calvert-Lewin or Semenyo is a more difficult selection call because Gameweek 1 has increased Zolis's appeal.

For midfield differentials, Tavernier is a credible 6.0m option with good underlying numbers, possible penalties when Klaassen is absent and appealing fixtures against Everton, Newcastle and Brentford. Yet Injae is preferred if he stays at Everton: he is first-choice for penalties, has no European schedule and is the stronger long-term wildcard option. Chelsea's Lacroix also appeals at 6.0m through secure minutes, defensive-contribution potential and attacking involvement, but managers uncertain of Chelsea clean sheets should not pay that price. Colwill, Reece James and cheaper defensive-contribution options may offer better value, particularly if Colwill returns from his knock.

Managers set up to Bench Boost in Gameweek 2 should generally play it rather than react to one poor week. Coventry's home match with Hull remains excellent on paper, Enzo Le Fee has penalties, and Petrovic's difficult opener comes away at Manchester City. If Palacios is fit, he is worth risking; if ruled out, replacing him and using the chip is preferred to rebuilding a strong bench later. Pedro Porro is an appealing replacement if ready to start, while Reece James, Xhaka and James Hill offer safer starts. Looking ahead, Haaland is the priority for Manchester City's Gameweek 3 home fixture, but Chelsea assets may be more dependable beyond that because Palmer and Joao Pedro have strong minutes and Chelsea have no Europe. Vissa is especially attractive from Gameweek 3 after playing in a No. 10 role for Newcastle, posting 0.94 xG against Liverpool and entering a favourable run of fixtures.
key_points: Captain Bruno Fernandes against Ipswich at home in Gameweek 2, with Haaland at Crystal Palace the main alternative and Palmer the differential choice if passed fit.
Do not overreact to Gameweek 1: continue targeting newly promoted Hull and Ipswich while using early performances only as supporting evidence.
Bench De Cuyper at Chelsea if you own home-fixture defenders such as Maguire, Ballard or Calafiori, despite De Cuyper's advanced left-wing role.
Prefer Everton's Injae over Bournemouth's Tavernier if Injae remains at Everton, chiefly for penalty duty, stronger fixtures and no European commitments.
Avoid rushing into 6.0m Lacroix until Chelsea's best defensive option is clearer; Colwill, Reece James and cheaper defenders may be better value.
Use a planned Gameweek 2 Bench Boost with Coventry defenders, Enzo Le Fee and Petrovic; replace injured Palacios rather than automatically postponing the chip.
Roll the transfer rather than sell Phil Foden for Dominik Szoboszlai before Gameweek 2, preserving flexibility for Gameweek 3.
Target Vissa from Gameweek 3 as a 6.0m Newcastle forward with strong minutes, possible penalties and fixtures including Bournemouth, Leeds, Hull and Coventry.

items.title: FPL GW2 TRANSFER TIPS! | Top Picks Tier List for Gameweek 2 - 2026/27! ⭐
items.headline: Haaland and Bruno Fernandes are Gameweek 2 holds as injury exits drive the transfer market
items.summary:
Gameweek 2 is not the time to burn transfers on one-week disappointment. Erling Haaland remains a clear hold despite blanking against Bournemouth: he records five shots, four in the box, one big chance and 0.85 non-penalty xG, with an additional offside chance not reflected in the data. Manchester City face an injury-hit Crystal Palace defence next, while Haaland owners have no sensible one-transfer upgrade. Alexander Isak is also worth keeping after posting 1.03 non-penalty xG and two big chances, even though Dominik Szoboszlai now appears to be Liverpool's first-choice penalty taker. Joao Pedro is the standout forward hold and buy at £7.5m, having been badly underpriced relative to his role and output.

The preferred Gameweek 2 captaincy options are Bruno Fernandes and Haaland, with Fernandes narrowly presented as the leading pick against Ipswich at home. Manchester United disappoint in Gameweek 1, but Bruno B. and Bryan Mbeumo still face a much better fixture and Mbeumo creates or reaches several promising situations. Pascal Gross is another hold after an unlucky display for Brighton, including a strong penalty claim, four key passes and near-misses in the box; Chelsea, Leeds and Coventry offer further upside. Do not rush to move Bruno or Mbeumo for Cole Palmer or Morgan Rogers: Palmer has a minor injury concern and Brighton away is not an obviously superior immediate fixture, while Chelsea's new arrivals are better reassessed after Arsenal in Gameweek 3.

Prioritise transfers for players with genuine availability problems. Ollie Watkins is a sell after missing Aston Villa's squad amid apparent exit talk, while Beto and Jorgen Strand Larsen are moved on if they remain second-choice options. In midfield, Sarr, Moises Caicedo and Bruno Guimaraes are higher-priority sales after failing to make their matchday squads; Morgan Gibbs-White also leans sell because of a possible injury, deeper role and weak Nottingham Forest projections. At the back, Pervis Estupinan, Pedro Porro and Micky van de Ven are sells because of fitness issues, with Van de Ven especially urgent. Gabriel, Luke Shaw and Harry Maguire are holds, supported by strong clean-sheet potential and attacking routes, while Arsenal's Riccardo Calafiori or Ben White are leading defensive buys.

Among new targets, Yoane Wissa stands out after four shots and 0.94 non-penalty xG in 90 minutes, with penalties likely and favourable Newcastle fixtures against Spurs, Bournemouth, Leeds and Hull. Kai Havertz is a viable Arsenal-forward alternative, while Callum Wilson and Thiago are safer but less compelling forward options to monitor. In midfield, Ibrahim Sangare offers cheap defensive-contribution points plus occasional attacking returns, Szoboszlai gains appeal as Liverpool's penalty taker, and Martin Odegaard looks promising at £6.5m in more advanced positions. Avoid chasing short-term returns from players with poor fixtures, uncertain minutes or transfer uncertainty, including Emerson, Evanilson, Gakpo and several Hull defenders. Save goalkeeper transfers unless a starter is unavailable; keep Lammens and Kinsky, but sell Emiliano Martinez or Guglielmo Vicario if their respective transfer situations remove them from contention.
key_points: Captain Bruno Fernandes or Erling Haaland in Gameweek 2, with Bruno favoured for Manchester United's home match against Ipswich.
Keep Haaland and Isak despite Gameweek 1 blanks because their chance data remains strong; do not downgrade Haaland simply to fund Isak.
Buy or hold Joao Pedro at £7.5m, while Yoane Wissa is the leading alternative forward target after 0.94 non-penalty xG and four shots.
Sell Watkins, Beto and Jorgen Strand Larsen if their minutes remain blocked, and prioritise injured or absent midfielders such as Sarr, Caicedo and Bruno Guimaraes.
Keep Gabriel, Shaw and Maguire; Calafiori and Ben White are the preferred defensive buys because Arsenal retain excellent clean-sheet odds.
Monitor Jean-Philippe Mateta, Cristhian Mosquera, Daniel Munoz and Eberechi Eze-style transfer or rotation situations before committing transfers.
Do not rush from Bruno or Mbeumo to Palmer or Rogers ahead of Gameweek 2; reassess Chelsea midfielders after their Arsenal fixture.
Avoid unnecessary goalkeeper moves, but transfer out Martinez or Vicario if they are no longer set to play.

items.title: My transfer tips ahead of Gameweek 2 #fpl #fantasypremierleague #fpltips
items.headline: João Pedro and Cole Palmer lead the Gameweek 2 watchlist, but patience is the transfer theme
items.summary:
João Pedro and Cole Palmer emerge as the standout attacking options after impressing against Fulham, with Morgan Rogers also offering strong value at £7.0m. All three look capable of becoming long-term FPL picks, particularly because their schedules are not complicated by European competition, but there is no need to force an immediate move before Gameweek 2. The recommendation is to reassess after Gameweek 3, when there is more evidence on roles and minutes.

Pascal Groß remains a hold despite blanking in Gameweek 1. His minutes appear secure, he is a likely penalty taker, and a favourable Gameweek 3 run of Leeds at home followed by Coventry away gives him a clear chance to repay patience. Kadioglu is another player with upside at his price if he continues on the left wing, although Mitoma's fitness is the decisive factor: once Mitoma is available, he is expected to reclaim first-choice status. Anderson's early departure against Bournemouth looks like cramp rather than an injury concern, so he remains a viable budget option for Gameweek 2.

There is less confidence in Chukwuemeka starting in Gameweek 2 despite a promising substitute appearance, making him a wait-and-see pick until Gameweek 3. Cody Gakpo appears to be Liverpool's most attractive midfield option from the opening evidence, but transfer rumours mean buying now carries unnecessary risk. Kai Havertz completing 90 minutes is encouraging, yet Gyökeres is still expected to challenge his role over the longer term.

Managers are urged not to panic-sell Bruno Fernandes or Bryan Mbeumo after an underwhelming opening result, with Ipswich at home offering a much better immediate test. Pedro Porro is also a hold where possible: many managers are selling, but an update from the manager could yet confirm his availability for Gameweek 2. Anyone who moved early for Conor at £4.5m should also hold for now, as regular minutes would make him exceptional value.
key_points: João Pedro and Cole Palmer are the preferred attacking targets after their Fulham performance, but both can wait until after Gameweek 3.
Morgan Rogers remains an appealing £7.0m value pick, although there is no urgency to buy him for Gameweek 2.
Keep Pascal Groß despite his Gameweek 1 blank because his minutes, possible penalties and upcoming Leeds and Coventry fixtures are attractive.
Do not rush for Kadioglu at left wing until there is clarity on Mitoma's fitness and likely return to the starting side.
Anderson is expected to be fit for Gameweek 2 after appearing to leave the Bournemouth match with cramp.
Avoid buying Cody Gakpo immediately despite his strong Liverpool midfield case, as speculation over a possible exit remains a risk.
Hold Bruno Fernandes, Bryan Mbeumo and, if already owned, Pedro Porro rather than reacting to one poor Gameweek 1 result.

items.title: TOP 3 FPL GW2 TRANSFER TARGETS! 🎯 #fpl #premierleague
items.headline: Mamadou Sangare leads Gameweek 2 shopping list after advanced role and two assists
items.summary:
Mamadou Sangare is the standout Gameweek 2 target after combining attacking output with strong underlying defensive work. Having initially been rated a “10 out of 10” pick for Gameweek 1, he was only omitted at the deadline to fund an upgrade in defence. Sangare then delivers two assists while registering 13 defensive contributions, and his advanced positioning strengthens the case that he offers exceptional value.

Martin Odegaard is another midfield option under consideration at £6.5m. Solis remains the preferred pick between the pair, but Odegaard becomes especially relevant as a possible downgrade from Bryan Mbeumo. Mbeumo fails to impress in Gameweek 1, and moving to Odegaard could release funds for upgrades elsewhere without abandoning a high-quality midfield asset.

Nico O’Reilly is the third target and may be the beneficiary of any Mbeumo downgrade. Manchester City concede and do not look completely secure defensively in Gameweek 1, but O’Reilly’s role is highly encouraging: he operates as the No. 10 and repeatedly arrives in dangerous attacking positions. The appeal is therefore based less on City’s clean-sheet potential and more on O’Reilly’s advanced role and route to attacking returns.

The transfer decision hinges on squad structure. Sangare is the priority value buy, while Odegaard offers a route out of Mbeumo and O’Reilly is the higher-upside attacking addition that extra budget could help finance. The main risk is reacting too strongly to one underwhelming Mbeumo performance, but his Gameweek 1 display makes a cheaper midfield alternative worth considering.
key_points: Mamadou Sangare is a leading Gameweek 2 target after two assists, 13 defensive contributions and an advanced role.
Sangare was originally rated a 10/10 Gameweek 1 pick but was sacrificed late to improve the defence.
Martin Odegaard costs £6.5m and is a potential Bryan Mbeumo downgrade if funds are needed elsewhere.
Solis remains the preferred midfield choice over Odegaard, but Odegaard suits a budget-saving transfer plan.
Nico O’Reilly plays as Manchester City’s No. 10 and consistently finds dangerous positions despite City’s imperfect defensive display.
Selling Mbeumo for Odegaard could create the money required to bring in O’Reilly.

items.title: MY FPL GW2 FIRST TRANSFER PLANS! 💥 #fpl  #premierleague  #gw2    #fantasypremierleague #football
items.headline: Bruno Fernandes keeps the armband as Manchester United triple-up gets Ipswich reprieve
items.summary:
The squad remains set up in a 3-4-3 for Gameweek 2 after a strong opening week, with more than 20 points available from the bench. The main selection question is in defence: Joe Rodon and Kristoffer Ajer face one another, and Rodon gets the nod because the home defender is preferred in an otherwise close call.

Manchester United’s poor Gameweek 1 display does not yet trigger a sale. A triple-up on United is retained for Ipswich at Old Trafford, with the fixture considered good enough to justify giving the players another week despite concerns over the previous performance. Bruno Fernandes remains captain, with Crystal Palace’s unconvincing form strengthening the case for backing him.

Erling Haaland is not trusted enough to take the captaincy at this stage, although that decision is revisited for Gameweek 3. The current preference is to hold the Manchester United assets and accept the risk that their Gameweek 1 issues carry over, rather than make a reactionary move before a favourable home fixture.

Brentford’s Sangari is a player of interest for future weeks, while a third Arsenal asset is also appealing despite Arsenal’s away match at Aston Villa. However, there is no obvious midfielder to sell for Sangari and no clean route to another Arsenal player. With the existing Arsenal double-up retained, rolling the transfer is prioritised over forcing a move.
key_points: Start Joe Rodon over Kristoffer Ajer in Gameweek 2, with the home-defender preference deciding a direct head-to-head fixture.
Keep the 3-4-3 formation after the bench delivers more than 20 points in Gameweek 1.
Hold the Manchester United triple-up despite a poor opener because Ipswich visit Old Trafford in Gameweek 2.
Captain Bruno Fernandes rather than Erling Haaland, with Crystal Palace viewed as an unconvincing opponent.
Reassess Haaland captaincy in Gameweek 3 rather than switching immediately.
Sangari of Brentford and a third Arsenal player are transfer targets, but no obvious route exists this week.
Roll the free transfer rather than weakening the squad to force in a Brentford or Arsenal asset.

items.title: CHELSEA ATTACK ON FIRE! 🔥 FPL GAMEWEEK 2 PREVIEW! 🔮 | Fantasy Premier League 2026/27
items.headline: Bruno Fernandes remains the Gameweek 2 captain as Arsenal and Chelsea attacks rise on the radar
items.summary:
Bruno Fernandes is the preferred captain for Gameweek 2 at home to Ipswich, and owners of Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and most other Manchester United starters are urged to hold for the same fixture. Even players who disappoint in Gameweek 1 should not trigger immediate sideways transfers: rolling a transfer is generally more valuable than reacting to one round of data. Morgan Gibbs-White and Phil Foden are closer to sells, but both are still worth considering as holds because of their fixtures and the lack of flexibility from having only one free transfer.

Arsenal remain the standout investment despite upcoming fixtures against Aston Villa and Chelsea. Their 3-0 opening win is backed by elite defensive numbers, with only 0.2 expected goals conceded, so the priority is Arsenal defence and midfield rather than their goalkeeper. Calafiori is the top target, followed by Ben White, as both combine clean-sheet potential with attacking involvement. Solanke is narrowly preferred to Martin Odegaard because his underlying output looks more repeatable, while Bukayo Saka is the premium option for set pieces, penalties when Viktor Gyokeres is absent, and Arsenal's central attacking role. Ezri Konsa should not be bought until he actually starts; reports of an immediate debut against his former club Aston Villa are treated as speculation.

Chelsea's 3-2 win over Fulham puts Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers on the watchlist, particularly because a back-five shape allows the three attackers to operate narrowly and combine centrally. Joao Pedro remains the best Chelsea pick, while Palmer and Rogers impress, but Brighton in Gameweek 2 and Arsenal in Gameweek 3 make this the wrong moment to rush into a double-up. Chelsea's defence is avoided while Robert Sanchez looks unreliable, although a cheaper goalkeeper such as Penders could eventually emerge. From Gameweek 4, Chelsea's fixture run makes a two-man attacking investment increasingly appealing.

Newcastle's performance against Liverpool makes Yoane Wissa a viable forward target despite a difficult trip to Spurs in Gameweek 2, with a favourable six-to-10-week run thereafter. Wissa plays centrally behind Osula and looks pivotal to the attack; Lewis Hall and Malick Thiaw are the defensive alternatives, although Newcastle still concede too many chances. Liverpool owners should also hold: Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak look concerning after underwhelming starts, and Dominik Szoboszlai's penalty may threaten Isak's spot-kick role, but Nottingham Forest, Ipswich and Fulham offer enough upside to give them at least another two matches. Gameweek 2 is also judged a poor time to wildcard, while managers who deliberately set up a Bench Boost with promoted-team players at home should still use it rather than abandon the plan after one poor week.
key_points: Captain Bruno Fernandes against Ipswich in Gameweek 2, and hold Mbeumo, Cunha and most secure Manchester United starters for the same fixture.
Prioritise Arsenal defenders Calafiori and Ben White, with Solanke, Odegaard and Saka the leading midfield routes into an elite defence and attack.
Do not buy Ezri Konsa until he starts an Arsenal match; his potential Gameweek 2 debut against Aston Villa is unsubstantiated.
Joao Pedro is the leading Chelsea asset, but wait through Brighton and Arsenal before aggressively targeting Palmer, Rogers or an attacking double-up.
Yoane Wissa is Newcastle's main transfer target after his advanced central role, while Lewis Hall and Malick Thiaw are longer-term defensive options.
Hold Liverpool assets Wirtz and Isak for Nottingham Forest, Ipswich and Fulham, despite Wirtz's modest data and uncertainty over Isak retaining penalties.
Avoid an early Gameweek 2 wildcard unless the squad is beyond repair; managers with a planned Bench Boost and playable home fixtures should stick with it.
The removal of dispossession penalties from the bonus system improves the appeal of dribbling wide players such as Iliman Ndiaye and potentially Solanke.

items.title: FPL GW2 TRANSFER TIPS ✅❌ Palmer IN? | Best Transfers
items.headline: Cole Palmer emerges as the Chelsea target, but Gameweek 2 calls for patience
items.summary:
Chelsea’s 3-2 win at Fulham strengthens the case for their attack, with Cole Palmer (13 points), João Pedro (11) and Morgan Rogers (eight) all impressing. João Pedro, priced at £7.5m and owned by 64.5%, looks a long-term hold after playing 90 minutes and benefiting from Chelsea’s lack of European football. Palmer is the premium target: he looks sharp after a summer off, has a history of 200-plus-point seasons and may retain penalties. However, Arsenal away in Gameweek 3 means there is no need to buy immediately; Brighton’s Gameweek 2 visit offers another data point before Chelsea’s stronger fixture run from Gameweek 4. Rogers is a viable cheaper route, particularly for managers selling a player such as Bryan Mbeumo, while Palmer suits those moving from Bruno Fernandes. Chelsea defenders are less appealing because the side still looks open and Robert Sánchez remains an error risk.

The central recommendation for Gameweek 2 is to avoid reacting to one match and roll a transfer where possible. Pascal Groß should be held despite blanking in Brighton’s 4-0 win: he plays 90 minutes, takes set pieces, may be first-choice penalty taker and has favourable Gameweeks 3-4. Hinshelwood’s two goals are encouraging, but his 63-minute outing despite a European midweek rest raises a minutes concern. Brighton defender De Cuyper is an exciting £4.5m option after playing on the left wing and recording a goal, assist and clean sheet, but his role depends on Kaoru Mitoma’s injury and potential transfer activity. Monitor him rather than buying before Chelsea away.

Manchester City options become more attractive from Gameweek 3, when fixtures improve. Elliot Anderson is a hold if fit after an early substitution that is attributed to cramp; at £6.5m he offers defensive-contribution potential, set pieces and some attacking involvement. Rayan Cherki’s two assists in 27 minutes show his quality, but his starting place is too uncertain to justify a Gameweek 2 transfer. Nico O’Reilly is the standout City defender to watch: the £6.5m player takes up advanced positions from left-back and looks more threatening from open play than Joško Gvardiol, although managers can wait until the home fixtures against Coventry, Sunderland and Ipswich begin.

Liverpool’s Gakpo is a wait because ongoing transfer speculation could radically change his minutes and role. Kai Havertz’s 90 minutes for Arsenal make him more attractive at £7.5m, but his security remains questionable with Viktor Gyökeres available and Arsenal still linked with another forward. Arsenal midfielders Zubimendi and Martin Ødegaard are strong £6.5m values but are not automatic buys after 75-minute appearances; their long-term appeal depends on transfer-window developments and whether managers prefer Arsenal’s exceptional defensive assets. Pedro Porro owners should wait for team news rather than sell after his Gameweek 1 absence: if fit, his fixtures and attacking role still make him viable, but an absence from the Gameweek 2 squad would justify a move.
key_points: Hold João Pedro and consider Cole Palmer from Gameweek 4, rather than forcing a Chelsea transfer before Arsenal away in Gameweek 3.
Most managers should roll their Gameweek 2 transfer rather than chase one-week returns or price rises.
Do not sell Pascal Groß after one blank; his set pieces, possible penalties and upcoming Brighton fixtures support a short-term hold.
Monitor De Cuyper’s left-wing role and Mitoma’s fitness, but avoid buying the £4.5m Brighton defender before Chelsea away.
Hold Elliot Anderson if Friday’s update confirms the issue is only cramp, while delaying Cherki decisions until his City minutes are clearer.
Target Nico O’Reilly from Gameweek 3 if his place holds, with City’s home games against Coventry, Sunderland and Ipswich approaching.
Avoid buying Gakpo until the transfer window closes, and wait for more clarity on Havertz, Ødegaard and Zubimendi’s Arsenal minutes.
Keep Pedro Porro unless Spurs confirm he remains unavailable; sell only if he misses the Gameweek 2 squad.

items.title: 15 things we've learned ahead of Gameweek 2 #fpl #fantasypremierleague #fpltips
items.headline: Salah penalty claim strengthens Liverpool captaincy case for Gameweek 2
items.summary:
Mohamed Salah may now be Liverpool’s first-choice penalty taker, a development that further elevates his captaincy appeal for Gameweek 2. Liverpool’s Florian Wirtz remains a high-upside option but carries an early-substitution risk, while Arsenal’s attacking hierarchy looks clearer: Viktor Gyökeres receives no minutes in Gameweek 1 and Kai Havertz appears to be the first-choice No. 9.

At Manchester United, Amad Diallo’s injury makes Bryan Mbeumo’s minutes look much safer, improving his appeal as a secure attacking pick. Martin Ødegaard also shows signs of returning to his best, while Nico O’Reilly plays as Manchester City’s No. 10 but is not viewed as a reliable long-term option given City’s depth and rotation risk.

Several budget midfielders emerge as potential transfers. Mamadou Sangare posts two assists and 13 defensive-contribution points in only 75 minutes, suggesting he could offer the kind of value previously associated with Elliot Anderson. Maxim De Cuyper, priced at £4.5m as a defender, plays at left wing for Brighton, while Diego Gomez records an assist after 85 minutes at £5.0m. Angulo also returns in Gameweek 1 at the same price, although his pre-60-minute substitution is a warning over his security of minutes.

The forward market is also shifting. Ollie Watkins misses Aston Villa’s squad amid indications he could be sold, and Ismaïla Sarr is similarly absent from Crystal Palace’s squad, making both situations worth monitoring before committing transfers. Yoane Wissa impresses against Liverpool and joins the viable £6.0m-forward bracket, while Barry and Oli McBurnie offer cheaper £5.5m routes to fund premium midfielders. The main trade-off is clear: the cheaper forwards and midfielders create squad flexibility, but several come with uncertain roles, substitution risk or transfer speculation.
key_points: Mohamed Salah may be Liverpool’s penalty taker, making him an even stronger Gameweek 2 captaincy option.
Florian Wirtz offers attacking upside but is vulnerable to early substitutions.
Amad Diallo’s injury improves Bryan Mbeumo’s prospects of secure minutes at Manchester United.
Mamadou Sangare records two assists and 13 defensive-contribution points in 75 minutes and emerges as a budget-midfield watchlist option.
Brighton defender Maxim De Cuyper plays at left wing, giving the £4.5m pick major out-of-position upside.
Kai Havertz looks Arsenal’s first-choice striker after Viktor Gyökeres goes unused in Gameweek 1.
Ollie Watkins and Ismaïla Sarr miss their clubs’ squads, with potential sales creating immediate uncertainty.
Yoane Wissa, Barry and Oli McBurnie provide viable cheaper-forward alternatives, with Wissa especially impressive against Liverpool.

items.title: TOP 30K 🌎🚀 | FPL GENERAL'S TEAM REVEAL GW2 🔥 |  FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Bruno Fernandes captaincy holds firm as Haaland owners resist GW1 panic
items.summary:
A fast Gameweek 1 Bench Boost start changes little in the immediate plan. A 71-point return, including 16 points from the bench through Kinsky, Rodon, Leif Davis and the late punt on Slater, is treated as a success, especially with Erling Haaland blanking as captain and Bruno Fernandes also failing to return. The key message is patience: one game is too small a sample to rip up a squad built around early captaincy fixtures.

Bruno Fernandes remains the preferred Gameweek 2 captain at home to Ipswich, with Haaland vice-captain away to Crystal Palace. Manchester United disappoint badly at Hull, but the fixture process still stands: United have back-to-back promoted sides, and a home reaction at Old Trafford is expected. Luke Shaw’s one-pointer is not a sell yet either, with four chances created offering encouragement, although he may later make way for a stronger Defcon-style defender such as Ajer or Rodon.

The Gameweek 2 team is set up to roll the transfer. Kinsky starts in goal at home to Newcastle ahead of Verbruggen away to Chelsea, while Shaw, Ben White and Calafiori form the back three. Odegaard, Mbeumo, Szoboszlai and captain Bruno sit in midfield, with Haaland, Joao Pedro and Calvert-Lewin up front. Rodon is first bench at home to Brentford, with Slater ahead of Leif Davis because of his set-piece role. Calvert-Lewin is held for now, but Newcastle’s Wissa is the forward who most threatens that spot if his strong underlying numbers continue.

Early watchlists are forming rather than triggering immediate moves. De Cuyper’s huge Brighton haul is acknowledged, but his minutes remain a risk when Mitoma returns, while Pascal Gross looks more secure after lasting well and moving into advanced areas late on. Rutter at Brighton, McBurnie at Hull and Forest’s Eager Jesus are monitored among cheaper forwards, while Brobbey’s Sunderland appeal fades after their fixtures turn. The captaincy route remains Haaland in Gameweeks 3 and 5, a Chelsea asset such as Joao Pedro or Cole Palmer in Gameweek 4, and potentially Saka after a Gameweek 6 wildcard if Arsenal’s fixtures and form align.
key_points: The transfer is rolled in Gameweek 2, with no immediate injuries or structural problems forcing action.
Bruno Fernandes is the Gameweek 2 captain at home to Ipswich despite Manchester United’s poor opening display at Hull.
Erling Haaland stays central to the plan, with captaincy earmarked for Gameweeks 3 at home to Coventry and 5 at home to Sunderland.
Luke Shaw is a hold for Ipswich but is already pencilled in as a possible future sale for a better Defcon defender such as Ajer or Rodon.
Calvert-Lewin is not sold after one blank, but Wissa is the standout forward replacement to monitor after Newcastle impress in Gameweek 1.
De Cuyper’s explosive Brighton return is treated cautiously because Mitoma’s eventual comeback could threaten his starts.
Joao Pedro or Cole Palmer is the early Gameweek 4 captaincy route when Chelsea host Hull.
Managers on the Gameweek 2 Bench Boost plan are advised not to abandon it solely because Hull beat Manchester United in Gameweek 1.

items.title: FPL PLAYERS TO BUY | GW2 ✅
items.headline: Bruno Fernandes edges Haaland as Gameweek 2 captain while Arsenal defence rises
items.summary:
Gameweek 2 is framed as a week for patience rather than panic. Big Gameweek 1 hauls from players such as De Cuyper, Hinshelwood, Mendy and Aït-Nouri are treated with caution because last week’s points cannot be bought back and many of those returns are unlikely to repeat immediately. If a squad is structurally sound, rolling a transfer is still a sensible route, even though early wildcards can work in extreme cases.

David Raya again leads the goalkeeper projections after Arsenal allow only 0.2 xG and four shots in Gameweek 1, strengthening the case that double Arsenal defence could become a key setup. The drawback is price and squad-slot pressure: on a Gameweek 2 wildcard, a cheaper keeper such as Sanchez or Petrovic may be preferable to preserve Arsenal spots for Gabriel, a 4.5m defender punt and a midfielder like Ødegaard or Saka. In defence, Gabriel tops the projections, Virgil van Dijk remains attractive at home to Nottingham Forest, and mid-priced options such as Antonio Silva, Thiaw and the Leeds defenders are flagged for defensive-contribution potential and fixtures.

Bruno Fernandes is the standout Gameweek 2 captain call despite blanking in Gameweek 1, with the projections placing him ahead of Erling Haaland. Haaland is still the main forward option and has an inviting fixture against a Crystal Palace side weakened by departures and injury, but Bruno’s home fixture and role make him arguably the safest armband. Dominik Szoboszlai also rises in appeal at 7.0m after taking a Liverpool penalty and sharing set pieces, while Bukayo Saka is highlighted as a high-upside, low-owned route into Arsenal for managers who can afford him.

The main message on premium forwards and midfielders is to hold nerve. Alexander Isak blanks in a hostile return to Newcastle but posts 1.1 xGI and has Ipswich in Gameweek 3, so he should be kept. Matheus Cunha is another straightforward hold after a disappointing one-pointer, while Florian Wirtz gets a couple more weeks because of the upcoming Ipswich fixture. Among cheaper midfielders, Sangare, Anderson, Ndiaye, Hinshelwood and Gomez all enter the watchlist, with Sangare’s defensive contributions raising his floor even if the attacking returns slow.

The no-Haaland structure remains viable because the money can be spread into combinations such as Isak, Palmer and Saka, but the risk is obvious: Haaland can punish non-owners with a haul at any time. The best projected Gameweek 2 squad even omits him, showing how competitive the alternatives are, but captaincy and team structure should be judged on repeatable roles, fixtures and minutes rather than one volatile opening round.
key_points: Bruno Fernandes is projected above Erling Haaland for Gameweek 2 captaincy and remains a strong pick despite his opening blank.
Rolling a free transfer is sensible for many teams, with the warning not to chase isolated Gameweek 1 hauls from defenders and cheap midfielders.
David Raya is the top goalkeeper projection, but wildcarders may prefer Sanchez or Petrovic to keep Arsenal slots open for outfield players.
Gabriel leads the defender projections, while Van Dijk at home to Nottingham Forest and 5.0m options such as Antonio Silva and Thiaw are notable alternatives.
Bukayo Saka is highlighted as a major upside pick at only around 10% ownership, though fitting him alongside Haaland and Bruno is difficult.
Dominik Szoboszlai looks a strong 7.0m option if he keeps penalties and set pieces for Liverpool.
Alexander Isak is a hold after strong underlying numbers and an Ipswich fixture in Gameweek 3, despite blanking at Newcastle.
Sangare, Anderson, Ndiaye, Hinshelwood and Gomez are the cheaper midfielders to monitor, with Gomez preferred among the 5.0m bracket.

items.title: FPL Gameweek 2 Early Thoughts 🔥 Szoboszlai essential? 🤔 Sell Wirtz? ❌
items.headline: Bruno Fernandes gets Ipswich captaincy nod as Gameweek 2 patience takes priority
items.summary:
Gameweek 2 is framed as a week for restraint: roll the free transfer wherever possible and take two moves into Gameweek 3. The logic is that Gameweek 1 squads are effectively wildcard-built for the opening fixtures, and one set of blanks is not enough evidence to rip up those plans. Exceptions exist, particularly if a non-playing pick such as Ismaila Sarr is at risk of leaving Crystal Palace and there is no bench cover, but the default move is to avoid early transfers, protect flexibility and reduce the need for hits later.

Manchester United assets are firm holds despite a poor 2-0 defeat to Hull. Bruno Fernandes, Bryan Mbeumo, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw all have Ipswich at home in Gameweek 2, a fixture strong enough to override one bad performance. Mbeumo’s underlying numbers are encouraging, with 0.5 xG and 0.23 xA, and Amad’s possible six-week absence should help his minutes, even if he is not playing as a No 9. Fernandes remains a viable captaincy option for Ipswich at home, even if premium alternatives impress elsewhere.

Liverpool’s situation is more nuanced. Florian Wirtz is a hold despite an early 62-minute substitution, with Forest at home in Gameweek 2 and Ipswich away in Gameweek 3 still too good to sell before gaining more information. Dominik Szoboszlai looks increasingly attractive after taking a high-pressure late penalty against Newcastle; at £7.0m, penalties, set pieces and a No 8 role with box threat make him outstanding value. Even so, chasing him immediately from Wirtz is not advised, particularly just to avoid price changes. Ekitike/Isak is also a hold for the next two fixtures, though his appeal drops if he is not Liverpool’s main penalty taker.

Mamadou Sangare emerges as a standout Brentford watchlist pick after 13 defensive contributions and two assists in 75 minutes against Spurs. At £5.5m he profiles like a possible Elliot Anderson-style value midfielder, combining DefCon points with some attacking output, and he is a strong replacement for Sarr if a transfer is necessary. Elsewhere, Brighton’s De Cuyper is intriguing after playing left wing as a £4.5m defender, but Chelsea away and future minutes risk temper the excitement; Hinshelwood’s brace is appealing but early substitutions remain a concern. Erling Haaland owners simply hold through Palace away, while non-owners likely need a plan to buy him for Coventry at home in Gameweek 3, where he is viewed as the clear best captain.

The current Gameweek 2 squad plan is to roll the transfer and captain Bruno Fernandes against Ipswich. Raya and Calafiori face Aston Villa away, with Ballard against Fulham and Maguire against Ipswich completing the defence. Fernandes, Mbeumo, Szoboszlai and Semenyo start in midfield, with Ekitike, João Pedro and Calvert-Lewin up front. The main dilemma is benching Zolis away to Villa despite his strong Gameweek 1, with Semenyo the only realistic alternative to drop; De Cuyper and Nico Williams stay benched because their fixtures are Chelsea away and Liverpool away.
key_points: Roll the Gameweek 2 transfer if possible, with two free transfers in Gameweek 3 seen as far more valuable than reacting to one week of data.
Bruno Fernandes is the preferred Gameweek 2 captain in the sample squad because Manchester United face Ipswich at home.
Manchester United assets such as Fernandes, Mbeumo, Maguire and Shaw are holds despite the opening defeat, as Ipswich at home remains a prime fixture.
Dominik Szoboszlai looks excellent value at £7.0m if he is Liverpool’s first-choice penalty taker, but selling Florian Wirtz for him immediately is not recommended.
Mamadou Sangare is a strong £5.5m watchlist pick and a sensible Ismaila Sarr replacement if Sarr is unavailable or sold.
Erling Haaland is a hold for owners and a priority buy for non-owners ahead of Coventry at home in Gameweek 3, where he is the standout captain.
Phil Foden is a hold for Palace away despite long-term Manchester City minutes concerns, while Rayan Cherki is only a watchlist option for now.
Zolis versus Semenyo is the main benching dilemma, with Zolis likely benched away to Aston Villa despite his strong Gameweek 1.
